findings.title: nil default_locale raises NoMethodError in fallback list
findings.body: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` is called before `.compact`, so if `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil (or SiteSetting is unavailable, e.g. during asset precompile/early boot or a misconfigured site), `nil.to_sym` raises NoMethodError and every translation lookup through the fallback chain blows up. Guard the value (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym`) before calling to_sym, and compact before uniq.

findings.title: Fallback locale keys may be strings, causing mismatched/unloaded locales
findings.body: `[](locale)` returns `[locale, ...]` without normalizing `locale` to a symbol. I18n may pass strings (e.g. 'de'), so the chain can contain a String while `ensure_loaded!`/`@loaded_locales` in translate_accelerator compares symbols (`config.locale`). This results in the same locale being loaded twice or not matched at all, and `uniq` failing to dedupe 'de' vs :de. Normalize with `locale.to_sym`.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache key ignores fallback chain / site default locale (multisite leakage)
findings.body: With fallbacks enabled, a translation result now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` in addition to `config.locale`, but the cache key is only `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. The LRU cache is process-wide, so in multisite (or after changing the site's default locale) a value resolved via one site's fallback chain will be served to another site/request with a different default locale, producing wrong-language strings. Include the fallback chain (or site identifier) in the cache key, or clear the cache when default_locale changes.

findings.title: Fallback locales only loaded in web requests
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is invoked solely from ApplicationController#set_locale. Code paths that set I18n.locale outside a controller (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console) will have the fallback locales unloaded, so lookups that should fall back to the site locale or :en will return missing-translation output instead. Loading should be hooked where locale is set globally (e.g. inside the patched translate/load path).

findings.title: ensure_loaded! initializes shared state outside the mutex
findings.body: `@loaded_locales ||= []` and the subsequent `include?` check run outside LOAD_MUTEX, so two threads can concurrently assign different arrays to @loaded_locales, losing load bookkeeping and causing duplicate/missed locale loads. Move the initialization and check inside the synchronized block.

findings.title: Hash subclass only overrides #[], other Hash API returns empty
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList` subclasses Hash but overrides only `#[]`; `fetch`, `keys`, `each`, `empty?` etc. still reflect an empty hash. Any I18n (or plugin) code that uses those methods on `I18n.fallbacks` will see no fallbacks, silently bypassing this feature. Also, defining it at top level without a namespace risks constant collisions.
